scope: RPC request dispatch/settlement and peer identity ownership; not the complete provider block
reproducedAndFixed: ClaudeProvider.send finally-stop deleted a pre-existing socket/registry after start rejected an identity collision. Track only successfully created paths; exclusive file creation also rejects a registry race and dangling symlink.
A parsed null RPC frame threw from the message event handler instead of being ignored.
A synchronous RPC send exception left its pending entry and abort listener behind.
A server-request callback resolving after close caused a second send exception and an unhandled rejection. Build one response, send once, and fail pending requests if sending fails.

functionReview.CodexAppServerClient.constructor: Malformed JSON and non-object frames, binary rejection, late socket errors and remote close. Fake WebSocket boundary; real Unix WebSocket handshake remains outside scope.
functionReview.CodexAppServerClient.request: Distinct IDs, exact params, out-of-order/unknown/duplicate replies, pre-abort, later abort, send throw and cleanup once. Optional signal remains optional.
functionReview.CodexAppServerClient.#onMessage: Result/error routing, notifications, ID zero, unknown IDs and missing method; no callback required for notifications.
functionReview.CodexAppServerClient.#handleServerReques: Custom result, thrown Error, fallback denial, unsupported method, close-before-resolution and failed send without retry.
functionReview.CodexAppServerClient.#failAll: Pending rejection and listener/map cleanup, including repeated close/error events. No internal Map introspection: repeated cleanup is observed through signal listener calls.
functionReview.ClaudePeerEndpoint.start: Actual disposable Unix socket, existing socket+registry collision, dangling registry symlink and injected registry creation race. Native provider sessions are not used.
functionReview.ClaudePeerEndpoint.#writeOwnedFile: Exclusive creation, private file modes, valid contents, partial write failure and descriptor closure.
functionReview.ClaudePeerEndpoint.stop/#removeOwnedFile: Owned socket/registry/key removal, exit listener removal, repeated stop, restart and preservation of identities created by a new owner after stop.
functionReview.ClaudeProvider.send caller: Real caller finally-stop path exercised through a collision; no message reaches a native session.
functionReview.test cleanup: Register both existing socket-test cleanup hooks before listen/start can fail; bound those tests to 2000ms. Do not assert incidental asynchronous response ordering.

stryker.snapshotNote: Both runs use the recorded source hashes. The strengthened Stryker test snapshot precedes the final cleanup-hook move and response-order relaxation; exact snapshots are archived. Final test hashes above apply to the separate mechanical replay below.

finalTreeReplay.timeoutReview: The seven process deadlines were exhausted by multiple sequential 1500ms test timeouts, not syntax errors. Replaying those same seven with a 20s process ceiling completed and reported testTimeoutFailure. They remain deadline detections, not ordinary assertion kills.

survivorReview.reason: Decrementing numeric RPC IDs still provides distinct IDs; positive ascending numbering is not part of the adapter contract.
Only the pre-abort fallback error explanation is empty when the signal reason is nullish; rejection remains.
Only the later-abort fallback error explanation is empty; cancellation and cleanup remain.
The send-error pending entry exists unless already settled by a synchronous event. In that case the Promise executor also ignores a subsequent throw; externally settled outcome is unchanged.
Removing only the typeof check still ignores parsed primitives through absent id/method properties; null remains separately rejected.
An id-less malformed hybrid with method plus result/error can be dropped instead of treated as a notification. Valid RPC responses and notifications are unchanged; not universally equivalent.
The internal METHOD_NOT_FOUND code is not exposed: the handler preserves its message but converts every exception to wire code -32603.
Collision explanation becomes empty; public CLAUDE_PEER_COLLISION and preservation of existing files remain checked.
Removing force only introduces ENOENT for an absent path; this per-file cleanup already catches it and continues.
force:false has the same absent-path behavior as mutant 119 under the existing per-file catch.

artifacts: Downloads/waga-qa-transport-2026-09-07-lwAoWT: raw reports, exact test snapshots, configs, locked tooling, mechanical replay scripts, TAP logs and standard verification logs
limitations: Timeout detection is reported separately from ordinary test failure; no combined score is presented as product reliability.
Ranges select only part of two files. Command runner does not distinguish uncovered mutants from survivors; this is not a provider-wide audit.
Live native agents, daemon handshake/restart, actual TUI behavior and model compliance were not tested. Existing user sessions and logs were not modified.
Provider ask completion/correlation/timeouts, usage caches, peer receive buffering/open-client shutdown and remaining connection boundaries stay in TODO.md.
The benchmark covers in-memory discovery and frame construction, not network/provider latency.
Hashes, dependencies, environment, test selection or config changes require reassessment; tests are not frozen.
